function.name: get_todays_events
function.description:
Retrieves today's calendar events. Use this when the user asks what's
    on their schedule, agenda, or calendar today.

function.name: add_calendar_event
function.description:
Add an event to the calendar.

    Args:
        title: The event's title.
        start: The event's start date/time.
        end: The event's end date/time. Defaults to one hour after start.
        description: Optional event description.
        location: Optional event location.
        recurrence: An RFC 5545 RRULE value if this event repeats — e.g.
            "FREQ=DAILY", "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR",
            "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2" (every two weeks), "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=15",
            "FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10" (stop after 10 occurrences), or
            "FREQ=WEEKLY;UNTIL=20261231T000000Z" (stop by a date, always UTC/"Z").
            Leave unset for a one-off event. A single reminder that happens once —
            even a relative one like "30 minutes before my appointment" — should
            use set_reminder instead, not a recurring event.

function.name: delete_calendar_event
function.description:
Delete an event from the calendar.

    Args:
        uid: The event's unique ID.

function.name: get_calendar_events
function.description:
Retrieves calendar events within a specific time range.

    Args:
        start: Start of the range.
        end: End of the range. A date alone (e.g. 2026-10-19) includes that whole day.

function.name: update_calendar_event
function.description:
Update an event in the calendar.

    Args:
        uid: The event's unique ID.
        title: The event's title.
        start: The event's start date/time.
        end: The event's end date/time.
        description: Optional event description. Omit to keep the current one.
        location: Optional event location. Omit to keep the current one.
        recurrence: An RFC 5545 RRULE value, same format as add_calendar_event.
            Replaces the event's recurrence outright — pass the existing value
            again to keep it, or omit to turn a repeating event into a one-off.

function.name: move_calendar_event
function.description:
Move an existing calendar event to a new start time, keeping its title
    and length. Use this to fix or change when an event happens.

    Args:
        event: The event's title (or part of it), or its UID.
        new_start: The new start date/time, as an absolute local date and time.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description:
Get the current weather.

    Args:
        location: City or suburb. Defaults to the user's configured location.

function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description:
Get the forecast weather for the next 7 days.

    Args:
        location: City or suburb. Defaults to the user's configured location.

function.name: get_range_forecast
function.description:
Get the forecast weather for a range of days.

    Args:
        start: Start date in ISO format (e.g., "2023-01-01")
        end: End date in ISO format (e.g., "2023-01-05")
        location: City or suburb. Defaults to the user's configured location.

function.name: add_planning_task
function.description:
Add one task with a time estimate to a day's planning note, for
    generate_schedule_blocks to arrange later. If the user lists several
    tasks at once, call this once per task, not a combined call.

    Args:
        task: A short description (e.g. "Kitchen dishes").
        duration_minutes: Estimated time to complete it, in minutes.
        date: The day this task is for, e.g. "2026-09-13". Defaults to
            today. Resolve relative language ("this Saturday") first,
            same as set_reminder.

function.name: generate_schedule_blocks
function.description:
Build a day's schedule: reads the planning note's tasks, merges
    them around that day's calendar events with breaks between sprints,
    writes the timeline into the note, creates a calendar event per
    block, and schedules an end-of-block reminder for each. Also returns
    a digest of the past week's filled-in "End of Day Reflection"
    entries, if any — factor that feedback into how you talk about the
    new schedule.

    Args:
        date: The day to schedule, e.g. "2026-09-13". Defaults to today.
        start_time: "HH:MM" (24-hour) to start scheduling from — use this
            instead of guessing when planning only part of the day (e.g. an
            evening after work). Defaults to the wake_time setting.
        end_time: "HH:MM" (24-hour) to stop scheduling at. Defaults to the
            bedtime setting.

function.name: set_reminder
function.description:
Set a one-off reminder for the user.

    Args:
        message: What to remind the user about.
        when: An absolute local date/time to fire the reminder (resolve
              relative language like "in 10 minutes" or "tomorrow at 9am"
              into an absolute date/time yourself first, per the date/time
              grounding rule).

function.name: set_timer
function.description:
Set a timer for the user — equivalent to a reminder with a default message.

    Args:
        when: An absolute local date/time the timer should go off (resolve
              relative language like "in 10 minutes" into an absolute
              date/time yourself first, per the date/time grounding rule).
        message: What to remind the user about. Defaults to a generic
                 "Timer's up!" message.

function.name: list_reminders
function.description: List the user's currently pending reminders.

function.name: cancel_reminder
function.description:
Cancel a pending reminder by matching text from its message.

    Args:
        message: Text to match against pending reminders' messages (a
                 substring is enough, e.g. "oven" matches "check the oven").

function.name: get_reflection_prompt
function.description:
Give the user a short grounding/reflection exercise when they ask
    for one directly (e.g. "give me a grounding exercise", "I need to
    check in with myself"). Relay the returned prompt conversationally —
    it already ends in a question. Separate from the app's randomized
    check-in schedule: doesn't create a scheduled check-in or affect
    today's count/cooldowns.

    Args:
        category: Optional effort level — "low" (quick grounding/somatic),
            "medium" (brief reflection), "high" (deeper values/self-efficacy
            reflection). Omit for a random one from any category.

function.name: jot_note
function.description:
Save the user's message as a quick note on today's capture list.
    Use it when they want something remembered or written down — a thought,
    an idea, something to do later, "note that...", "remember to..." — and it
    is not a calendar event, a timed reminder or a timer. Takes no arguments:
    the app saves their exact words.

function.name: fetch_webpage
function.description:
Fetch a specific webpage and extract its actual main content (not
    navigation, ads, or sidebar chrome) as clean text via boilerplate
    removal, not just an HTML-to-markdown dump. Use this after search_web
    when a result's snippet is only a pointer to what you need — a blurb
    saying a page has a full timeline/list/figures — rather than the detail
    itself, so you can read the real content instead of just relaying a
    link back to the user.

    Args:
        url: The exact URL to fetch, usually taken from a search_web result.

language.description:
Language code for results (e.g., 'en', 'en-US', 'fr', 'de').
     Use None for no language preference.

time_range.description:
Time range filter ('day', 'week', 'month', 'year').
       Use None for no time filtering.

safesearch.description: Safe search filtering (True to enable, False to disable)

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)
